description: Dependency updates for the music-management monorepo. Every ecosystem in here (pip, npm, Gradle, Dockerfile) is picked up automatically; the rules below only decide how the updates are grouped and how eagerly they are merged.

packageRules.description: A version published minutes ago can be unpublished, yanked or found compromised in the days after, and this repository merges several ecosystems automatically. Three days is long enough for that to surface and short enough that nothing waits a week; vulnerabilityAlerts above is scheduled at any time and is not held up by it.
Patch and minor updates of the Python runtime stack move together: they are covered by the unit suite and reviewing them one by one is noise.

A major of fastapi/pydantic/sqlalchemy is a migration, not an update. It opens on its own like everything else, but never merges on its own -- no automerge rule below matches a pip major -- and the label is so it is recognisable as a migration at a glance rather than something to wave through.

yt-dlp ships breaking extractor fixes as ordinary releases; being behind on it is what actually breaks downloading. Merge automatically once the pipeline is green, and exempt it from the repo-wide cooldown -- a three-day wait here is three days of failing downloads. One group, because the version is pinned in three places -- requirements.txt and the `# renovate:` ARGs in docker/Dockerfile.downloader and docker/Dockerfile.tools -- and they have to move in the same merge request.

pytest is capped below 9.2 in requirements.txt and tests/bdd/requirements.txt: 9.2 removed FixtureManager._arg2fixturedefs, which pytest-bdd 8.1 uses, and every BDD test fails in setup. Without this rule Renovate proposes the 9.2 bump again on every run. Lift the cap (and this rule) when pytest-bdd supports pytest 9.2.
Dev tooling is not shipped to production; an upgrade can only turn the pipeline red, never break a user.
Frontend dev dependencies move fast and are covered by lint + typecheck + vitest.

@playwright/test brings its own Chromium, and a new Chromium renders text a hair differently: the screenshot suite (docs/frontend-screenshots.md) goes orange on every route, which the soft gate would let through with stale references. Kept out of the group so the bump is one MR that refreshes the references before it merges.

Frontend runtime dependencies are covered by the same gates as the dev ones -- vitest, typecheck, lint and frontend:browser all run against the built app, so a break here is a red pipeline rather than a bad deploy.
muma-mobile's dependencies live in a version catalog and move as one group; reviewing an androidx patch bump by hand is noise. Covered by muma-mobile:check.
A Gradle major is AGP, Kotlin or media3 changing its API. Labelled and left ungrouped for the same reason as the Python majors above: it opens by itself, it never merges by itself.

Test and lint libraries are not in the APK, so the worst a bad one can do is turn muma-mobile:check red -- which is the check. Majors included, for that reason.

This list is explicit rather than a match on testImplementation, and the reason is the version catalog: Renovate updates a shared version.ref, not a single coordinate. kotlin-test-junit and kotlin-reflect ride on the same `kotlin` ref as the compiler, kotlinx-coroutines-test on the runtime coroutines, and mockwebserver on okhttp. Matching those by their test-sounding names would automerge a Kotlin compiler upgrade. They stay in the runtime group above on purpose.

TypeScript 7 is the native rewrite, and svelte-check does not accept it as a plain upgrade yet: it refuses to start unless TypeScript 6 is installed alongside it under an npm alias and every invocation passes --tsgo. That is a toolchain migration, not a version bump, so it waits on the dashboard until svelte-check can consume TypeScript 7 on its own.

Base image bumps rebuild every service image, so they are reviewed by hand -- which is what an unmerged merge request already is. Nothing here automerges; the label is what makes them stand out from a library bump in the list.

Images that used to float on :latest (or on a bare tag like nginx:alpine) are pinned to a version and a digest. pinDigests keeps it that way when Renovate rewrites the line, and for autoheal, which publishes no version tags, the digest is the only pin there is.

MariaDB is the production database. A minor or major moves the data directory (mariadb-upgrade, run by the entrypoint through MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE) and only reaches production on a DEPLOY_DB=1 deploy, after the pre-deploy dump -- the operator's runbook, "Moving MariaDB to a new version". Labelled so it is never waved through as an ordinary base-image bump, and held for a week rather than three days: a data-directory upgrade is the one update here that is hard to take back. Like every docker update here it never merges on its own.

deno is pinned together with the sha256 of its release zip (docker/Dockerfile.downloader). Renovate can bump the version but not the checksum, so its merge request goes red on `sha256sum -c` until DENO_SHA256 is filled in by hand -- see the operator's runbook, "Pinned build inputs". It never merges on its own.

The ml-analyzer is deprecated and disabled, its code kept for a possible revival (services/ml-analyzer/DEPRECATED.md). It is not built, deployed or tested by default, so a dependency merge request for it would be reviewed and merged for nothing. Remove this rule when the service is revived.
Vendored upstream fork; its dependencies are managed by that project, not here.

Exception to the rule above: services/music-management-server/docker-compose.yml is this repository's own production stack for LMS, not upstream's, and its autoheal and nginx images are pinned by digest. Without this they would stay on the digest of the day they were pinned.

customManagers.description: The default Python image of the local lint/typecheck container must move with the images (tests/ci/test_gitlab_ci_policy.py::test_ci_python_is_the_python_the_images_run); the Dockerfile managers do not read shell scripts.
